purpose: Targeted Protected Mode Ghidra audit of the shared eight-byte scheduler entry used by 0E96, 0FA2, 0FDC, and 1036.

source.independent_project_check: passed; project-a and project-b outputs matched

entry_layout.name: phase_callback_offset
entry_layout.operation: 0E96 reads the word, tests FFFF, and calls AX after filtering object +0x17 by phase; 1036 writes object +0x18 here
entry_layout.return_flags: the phase callback's flags are not consumed by 0E96

entry_layout.name: secondary_callback_offset
entry_layout.operation: 0FA2 loads this word into AX, skips zero, and calls AX with near CALL; 0FDC tests it for presence; 1036 writes object +0x1C here
entry_layout.return_flags: the secondary callback's flags are not consumed by 0FA2

entry_layout.name: object_offset
entry_layout.operation: 0E96, 0FA2, and 0FDC load this word into DI; 1036 writes DI here

entry_layout.name: entry_word_06
entry_layout.operation: not read or written by 0E96, 0FA2, 0FDC, or 1036

calls: near entry +0x00 callbacks in phase 0, 1, and 2 order
near entry +0x02 callback through CALL AX
fixed far import at 1024 when object +0x12 bit 0x8000 is clear

function_contracts.return: RETF at 1066, or early RETF at 103E

simulation_consequence.confirmed: A platform and player phase callback can execute in the same 0E96 pass in their object-phase order; 0FA2 is a later secondary-callback pass.
simulation_consequence.player_feedback: The scheduler has no direct player-record write. Platform 9DC7 can publish DS:5006/DS:8812/DS:8816, and the phase-ordered player 3FF8 callback can consume it.
unresolved: runtime bank membership after death/reload, detachment, and culling
